explanation: The execution contains a fault because the original corpus has eight qualifying demand records, all with demand_score >= 3, including n06-r06. Job 2 only received seven needs/evidence_sources and its observed output omits n06-r06. The downstream map_coverage function would allow n06-r06 if present, but the upstream normalize function's allowed_record_ids list omits n06-r06 and includes n06-r09 instead, causing the valid stipulated record to be silently dropped before the handoff.
cited_evidence: top_level_input includes n06-r06 with demand_score 5 and need 'compare selected and complete runtime evidence'.
select_demand selects records where demand_score >= 3, so n06-r06 qualifies.
normalize source has allowed_record_ids ['n06-r01','n06-r02','n06-r03','n06-r04','n06-r05','n06-r09','n06-r07','n06-r08'], omitting n06-r06.
job_2 input needs and evidence_sources contain n06-r01, n06-r02, n06-r03, n06-r04, n06-r05, n06-r07, and n06-r08, but not n06-r06.
map_coverage allowed_record_ids includes n06-r06, so the downstream code is not the point where n06-r06 was filtered out.
